name: FL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~4%
No polling available, but no evidence of a competitive race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Patronis: an R+18 district, incumbency, and a fundraising edge of more than 20-to-1, with outside groups also spending heavily for him. Markets price Valimont's chances near zero, and nothing in the evidence suggests movement toward her.
model.watch: A surprise polling error or a late scandal could narrow the margin, but flipping the seat would require an unprecedented shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Florida's 1st District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and incumbent Jimmy Patronis enters the general election with every structural advantage. He has raised nearly $3.8 million and holds over $930,000 on hand, while Democrat Gay Valimont has raised about $174,000 with modest outside support. No outside spending is targeting Patronis in any meaningful way.

Prediction markets give Valimont only a small chance of winning, and no public polling suggests the race is competitive. The forecast expects Patronis to win by roughly seventeen points, consistent with the district's strong Republican lean, though a strong Democratic environment could trim the margin somewhat.
